info.bio: Banda estadounidense de música pop. Formado el 20 de abril de 1993 en Orlando, sus miembros iniciales fueron Nick Carter, Howie Dorough, A. J. McLean, Kevin Scott Richardson y Brian Littrell. El 26 de Junio de 2006, Kevin Richardson anunció que dejaría la banda. Los Backstreet Boys son la mayor «boyband» que sigue en activo en el mundo, ya que han vendido más de 130 millones de discos. Actualmente llevan 20 años de carrera e influyeron en el surgimiento de bandas como *NSYNC y Westlife.

podcast.title: CD Sales - Multi-Million Copies
podcast.body: During the 1990s, artists like Backstreet Boys sold millions of copies of their CDs, which were considered sacred objects for expressing identity. This generated multi-million dollar revenues for the music industry. "Música están distintos como Alejandro San, Madonna, Baxter Boyz, orbejo Chile Peppers, vendían millones y millones de copias de esos objetos brillantes, generando ingresos multimillonarios."

podcast.body: Electronica was seen by critics in the late 1990s as the potential savior for alternative music from the perceived ruin caused by pop acts like the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears. "This, the critic said, was going to be the thing that saved the world of alternative music from ruin at the hands of the Backstreet Boys and Britney Spears and their ilk in the late 1990s."

podcast.title: Pop Music Decline
podcast.body: The Backstreet Boys were part of a group of pop artists from the mid-90s whose audience, by the mid-2000s, had grown older and began seeking angrier, more expressive music. This shift contributed to the rise of bands like Alexis on Fire. "But during that time, we were seeing the end of the spike in pop music, you know, the back street boys and instincts and Christine Aguilar is in Britney Spears and that group of people who had been into pop since the middle 90s with spice girls and whatever, they were now getting older and they were getting angry and they were looking for something that spoke to that anger and their fears and their frustrations."

xref.title: Pop Music Shift
xref.body: The rise of Alexis on Fire and similar aggressive bands coincided with a shift in pop music in the mid-2000s. Fans who had grown up with pop acts like Backstreet Boys, N'Sync, Christina Aguilera, and Britney Spears from the mid-90s were aging and seeking music that expressed anger, fears, and frustrations, creating an opening for bands like Alexis on Fire and Billy Talent. "But during that time, we were seeing the end of the spike in pop music, you know, the back street boys and instincts and Christine Aguilar is in Britney Spears and that group of people who had been into pop since the middle 90s with spice girls and whatever, they were now getting older and they were getting angry and they were looking for something that spoke to that anger and their fears and their frustrations."
